what: Hit rate of the direction-of-travel near-side rule against the calibrated near limb, 11 spent MoVi PG1 subjects.
rule: rightward travel across the image -> RIGHT side faces the camera; leftward -> LEFT. From left = superior x anterior in the OpenCV camera frame (x right, y down, z into scene).
travel_measured_from: the detected 2D only -- no depth, no calibration
diagnostic_only: all 11 subjects are spent; this establishes no held-out claim
aggregate_only: no per-subject MoVi value is written here, same standard as the scoping files
mirroring: the rule inverts under mirroring, which cannot be detected from the image; the demo warns and the filming instructions say to use the rear camera
reading: The rule ABSTAINED on 5 of 11 clips and was correct on 6/6 of those it answered. Forced to answer on all it would score 8/11, so the ambiguity floor is doing real work. The hit rate of 6/11 counts every abstention as a miss, which is the conservative reading. MoVi's jogging windows carry very little net horizontal travel -- subjects jog within a lab volume rather than crossing the camera's view -- so this is a floor set by the test footage, not a measurement of the geometry.
